mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines over the prior month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% over the prior month indicates a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in >60% of instances when UNRATE falls below 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) above its 3-month average and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 3-month average signals a shift from manufacturing to housing-led growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >60% of instances when HOUST rises above 3-month avg and INDPRO falls below 3-month avg, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2.0% signals robust corporate earnings momentum, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of late-cycle expansion periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in industrial production (INDPRO) over the prior month indicates strengthening manufacturing activity and economic growth, supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of periods when INDPRO rises over the prior month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 1.0% over the prior month signals monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises above 1.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% and unemployment rate (UNRATE) decline exceeding 0.2 percentage points indicate a rapidly tightening labor market, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >60% of instances when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% and UNRATE falls by >0.2pp, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During housing booms, housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month average signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of housing boom periods (HOUST > 12-month avg), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
